gist: Jordi Visser argues AI is 'destroying capitalism' by making moats and long-term cash flows unknowable, driving structural multiple compression and AI-linked cyber fears behind the sell-off (Nvidia ~40% off highs) despite intact fundamentals and a successful Anthropic IPO. He frames Bitcoin as the purest AI trade with tokenization as the long-run bridge, but stays out until Bitcoin and major indices reclaim their 200-day averages, watching for a breadth thrust, Fed softening and a year-end pain-trade rally.

themes.theme: AI uncertainty breaking long-term capitalism and institutional investing

insights.claim: Jordi Visser says institutional money managers are the most beaten-up and despondent he has ever seen, after a huge deleveraging phase with funds facing closure and redemptions, even though fundamentals and the economy have not changed.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Extreme institutional despondency is a contrarian sentiment signal; watch for capitulation-driven bottoms.
insights.quote: The institutions are beaten. I I'm not sure I've ever seen um institutional managers this beaten up.

insights.claim: Visser argues AI is destroying capitalism because model release speed makes competition for any idea infinite, so no business can build a durable moat; the future looks like serial entrepreneurship and revenue streams rather than long-lived companies.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Discount durable-moat assumptions for software/app businesses; favor firms with non-AI barriers.
insights.quote: there's just no way to create some to to have an idea that has enough time to create a mode.

insights.claim: Visser contends that because AI cuts off confidence in years five through twenty of discounted cash flows, equity multiples will structurally compress for a long time, and he would not rule out the S&P 500 trading at a single-digit P/E (e.g., 9) even as earnings keep growing.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect returns to lag earnings growth; valuation-based dip buying is less reliable in this regime.
insights.quote: I think multiples are compressing for a long time. I don't think you can even take single-digit pees out of the S&P in the world that I see.

insights.claim: Visser predicts that by 2030 there will be essentially no growth in public companies except a few with uncompetable moats such as Eli Lilly and SpaceX.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Concentrate long-duration equity exposure in businesses with regulatory/physical moats.
insights.quote: by 2030, I don't think there's going to be any growth in in public companies anymore.

insights.claim: Visser says Nvidia's multiple has fallen from about 70 during the AI bubble to close to 10, roughly a 40% discount to two to three months ago despite growing earnings, while Apple trades near 50x because it is a boring, undisrupted quality business — showing the market now pays for certainty, not growth.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The market is pricing disruption risk over growth; 'boring quality' commands a premium vs. AI compute names.
insights.quote: Why is Apple trading at a 50p and Micron is trading lower?

insights.claim: Visser asserts that the wave of outages and hacks (Microsoft outages, an FAA nationwide ground stop, bank and ATM problems, Apple outages, Japanese hacks) is AI-related, either directly from AI-driven hacking or from rushed patching that opens new vulnerabilities.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Cyber risk is now a market-wide uncertainty factor contributing to multiple compression; watch cybersecurity and bank deposit data.
insights.quote: Anyone who says these are not AI related is out of their mind.

insights.claim: Visser claims the only defense against AI agent swarms is defensive agent swarms, which are not ready, and says Anthropic's Mythos model was never released because of its risk while unreleased models are roughly twice as capable as current ones.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Cyber defense via AI agents is an under-built need; expect continued vulnerability while labs let firms patch.
insights.quote: The only way to protect against the agent swarms is to have agent swarms protecting against the agent swarms.

themes.theme: AI stock correction vs. intact fundamentals

insights.claim: Pompliano lists AI stock drawdowns from highs: Iren down 75-80%, Applied Digital 72%, Nebius 65%, CoreWeave 65-70%, Arm 60%, Super Micro 54%, Vertiv 50%, Micron 45%, Nvidia 40%, even as revenue and guidance keep rising.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: AI infrastructure names have been de-rated heavily despite fundamentals — a potential list for a rebound once technicals turn.

insights.claim: Visser says Nvidia has fallen from about 240 to 145 (roughly a 35-40% correction), and the broad market was down about 8.5-10% from highs — normal for the broad market but abnormal for AI names, which had risen far more.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Broad index damage is modest; pain is concentrated in AI leaders that retail widely owns.

insights.claim: Visser argues the AI flywheel is intact: better models drive better applications, more adoption and more compute demand, and at the Tomorrow X Summit every company said compute demand exceeds supply while Micron has missed nothing.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Compute demand fundamentals remain strong; the drawdown is a multiple, not an earnings, story.
insights.quote: Every single company that came to the stage, demand is greater than supply and compute.

insights.claim: Visser says Google Gemini went from no releases for about seven months to four releases in a month, and its models now have a distinct, less appeasing conversational voice; Pompliano notes Google, Alibaba and ByteDance video models ranked above OpenAI, with Anthropic absent, showing leadership can flip from threat to tailwind within one quarter.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: AI model leadership is unstable; avoid assuming durable consumer lock-in for any lab.
insights.quote: the threat can go from a threat to a tailwind back to a threat in one quarter

insights.claim: Visser maintains Eli Lilly will become the biggest company in the world because it sells longevity, benefits from AI model intelligence, and is protected by FDA approval and manufacturing barriers that AI cannot shortcut.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Favor AI beneficiaries with regulatory moats such as large pharma.
insights.quote: I would say and still say Eli Liy will be the biggest company in the world

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO and the shift to completed tasks

insights.claim: Visser calls the Anthropic IPO a success: it priced around the mid-80s, popped to 115-120, closed in the 90s and still traded near a $2 trillion valuation on day one.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Despite the fade, demand for mega AI IPOs held; quarterly reporting will now reveal growth trajectory.

insights.claim: Visser argues Anthropic's quarterly reporting removes a major cloud of uncertainty because investors can now see in real time whether the fastest-growing company ever is peaking; he believes its business is thriving and it sells billions of dollars of intelligence to enterprises like Eli Lilly rather than small businesses.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Anthropic earnings become a key AI-demand barometer for the whole trade.

insights.claim: Citing Druckenmiller at the Tomorrow X Summit, Visser says AI is moving from tokens to completed tasks, which should deliver Fortune 500 productivity gains, keep profit margins at record highs, and support about 15% S&P earnings growth next year, putting a floor under stocks.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch enterprise productivity and margins; 15% EPS growth is his base case for next year.
insights.quote: we're moving from tokens to completed tasks.

insights.claim: Visser finds it unthinkable that the Fed is still discussing rate hikes with core CPI at 2.6% amid this panic, and expects a shift soon — even just Fed governors moving from talking 50 to saying 25 is enough would be a good liquidity point.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A dovish Fed pivot in rhetoric is a key catalyst for risk assets.
insights.quote: It's unthinkable to me that you could have this kind of sentiment shift, this kind of panic going on and we're still talking about rate hikes with core CPI at 2.6%.

insights.claim: Visser frames Bitcoin, gold and stock multiples as driven by real two-year rates: two-year yields near 4.9% minus swap-implied inflation expectations near 2.3% give a roughly 2.6% real rate, which is bearish; he says Bitcoin has only been worth owning since 2014 when real two-year rates fall.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Track the two-year yield minus inflation swaps spread as the macro timing signal for Bitcoin.
insights.quote: the only time over the course of, you know, since 2014 has been when real two-year rates are going down.

insights.claim: Visser says global hard currency is about $120 trillion versus roughly $900 trillion of total assets, so the system is levered; he believes we are in a leverage unwind in which asset correlation with money supply (M2) will break down while correlation with liquidity holds.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Stop using M2 charts; use cross-asset liquidity measures during deleveraging.

insights.claim: Visser built a liquidity monitor of six pillars and 34 indicators back to 2014, and argues the best time to buy Bitcoin is when the market demands cash (stronger dollar, weak credit, rotation from beta to quality), because that marks proximity to a bottom.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use cash-demand extremes as accumulation windows for Bitcoin.

themes.theme: Bitcoin: purest AI trade, tokenization, and 200-day discipline

insights.claim: Visser calls Bitcoin 'the purest AI trade' because AI is driving both multiple compression in public equities and pervasive hacking, while Bitcoin has never been hacked and cryptography is becoming more important.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Bitcoin is positioned as a hedge against AI-driven equity de-rating and cyber insecurity.
insights.quote: I've called Bitcoin the purest AI trade.

insights.claim: Visser argues that if public equities and bonds (about $250-300 trillion of $900 trillion in assets) stop growing because of multiple compression, money will migrate to what is growing via tokenization, which he calls the inevitable bridge between fiat assets and Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Tokenization infrastructure and on-chain assets are the long-term beneficiaries of capital rotation.
insights.quote: Tokenization is going to happen. It is inevitable.

insights.claim: Visser will not buy Bitcoin aggressively until it reclaims its 200-day moving average (about 72-73k versus about 60k now), citing an 11-for-11 record of positive returns 120 days after Bitcoin regains the 200-day in broad-risk periods.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use a 200-day MA reclaim (~72-73k) as the trigger for Bitcoin exposure, possibly via upside options.
insights.quote: Until Bitcoin's back above the 200 day moving average, I don't give a crap about anything I just said to you.

insights.claim: Galaxy research (Alex Thorn) shows advisers and wealth platforms are the fastest-growing holders of spot Bitcoin ETPs, roughly tripling their share since Q1 2024, and Visser adds that IBIT shares outstanding and digital-asset-treasury company holdings are near all-time highs.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Sticky allocator flows keep building beneath weak prices — supportive for eventual recovery.

themes.theme: Tactical playbook: 200-day breaks, thrust signals and the year-end pain trade

insights.claim: Visser's rule: when SPY, QQQ and IWM all close below their 200-day moving averages at the same time as the bank index, he stops trading, closes positions, and only attempts bottom-picks on reversal days.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A simple multi-index 200-day filter for risk-off; current readings say the market is in trouble.

insights.claim: Visser is waiting for a breadth thrust — a day where the S&P rallies about 2% with roughly 90% of stocks up — ideally coinciding with Fed softening and a weaker dollar, as the trigger to add equity exposure from fixed income.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch for a 90% up-volume/breadth day as the actionable bottom signal.

insights.claim: Visser predicts the ultimate pain trade is a sharp year-end rally that beaten-up funds do not participate in, after which next year starts with uncertainty still unresolved.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Be positioned for an underowned year-end rally rather than further collapse.
insights.quote: the ultimate pain trade is that the market has a big rally into the end of the year.
